## The Bulb Test

Two metal rods called **electrodes** are joined to a battery and a small bulb, and they dip into a glass of pure water. The bulb stays dark. Now you stir a spoonful of salt into the water until it disappears, and you do the same with sugar in a second glass of pure water.

**Predict:** What will the bulb do in each glass?

options.text: Both glasses light the bulb, because dissolving any crystal sets electric charges free.
Only the salt water lights the bulb. The sugar water stays dark.
Neither glass lights the bulb, because dissolving is only a physical change.
